body:
Alex Gross, alexilen@sprynet.com, wrote on Sun, 10 Oct 1999:

> Well, here's where i get around to replying to some of your
> comments about my Images & Analogies piece.  Mostly to Patrick
> Juola this time around, as he managed to say so many silly things
> that there's no way i can chase them all down.  [...]

Buttinski Murray here -- quite a good read, Alex -- your 37-Amiga-
screen diatribe.  And thanks for all that background work on
Patrick Juola, with whom I have been in extreme mutual antagonism
over the past five years, fanned recently (29 April 1999) to a
white heat of intensity when he and 196 other fascisti had the
gall to vote in favor of moderating the comp.ai newsgroup.
(Could you please look up those other 196 pusillanimalities
and provide on them as thorough a background as on Patrick Juola?
Some of them will be hard to find because their names are very
spurious, like "Deep Thought" or ... aw, gee, I can't find my
list of the 197 enemies-of-the-people who voted for censorship.)

Patrick Juola certainly has a linguistics background -- based on
your gumshoery at the NYU library -- but he also insists that he
is a mathematician.  Maybe the twain have met, in Patrick's case.

Say, in your Unabomber episode, did you ever come across my post
of Sep 1995 predicting that the Unabomber would be a mathematician?


>    The Unabomber is a mathematician.

>    His so-called manifesto is freely available on the Internet at
> "http://pathfinder.com" as a 221,188-byte file of ASCII text with
> NUMBERED paragraphs.

>    The mathematical Unabomber writes in paragaph 17 of  "rational
> calculation," and in paragraph 39 of "the pursuit of goal X."  In
> paragraph 57, the mad bomber speaks of "a new, ordered community"
> which a non-mathematician would have called an orderly community.
> In paragraph 99, the cowardly killer writes, "Think of history as
> being the sum of two components...."  (Think, rather, of the Una-
> bomber as being a mathematician who uses perhaps a permutation of
> his own national identification  number as an authentication code
> in dealing with The New York Times.)   The mathematical psychotic
> continues in paragraph 143:   "In the past, human nature has been
> approximately  constant, or at any rate  has varied  only  within
> certain bounds."  Q.E.D.


People reacted angrily back then when I dared to predict what in fact
turned out to be true when the FBI arrested a Harvard mathematician,
and now I get the same antagonism from the likes of Patrick Juola
with respect to my predictions of how we will accomplish AI and MT.

http://www.geocities.com/Athens/Agora/7256/mind-fpc.html Mind.Forth
has some math problems in it, and I call upon all the David Hilberts
and Henri Mersennes of our day to help in finding the proper values
to plug into the SPREADACT routine where the AI associates concepts.

Finally, before I yield the floor to the "kitten" from Colorado,
please observe the results of my wining and dining a Japanoise
who aided and abetted me in translating a Mentifex mind-diagram.

Her face flushed with pleasure when I confided, "By the way,
your code name in my diaries is Dakota," and she still calls
herself "Dakota" in her e-mails from Tokyo.  (She looks like
Yoko Ono, who with John Lennon lived in the Dakota Apartments.
They all get code names, like "Bionica" or "Odna Mona.")

Now, Alex, a lot of the hits on the Mind.Forth Web site have
been coming from Japan.  Maybe the Japanese see some value in:

Chokaku = audition, hearing
Doshi = verb(s)
Gainen = concept; notion, general idea [not used here]
Gakusetsu = theory, doctrine
Keiro = channel; course, stage; process
Kioku = memory
Kotoba = word(s)
Meishi = noun(s)
no = [possessive particle] "of"
Shikaku = sight, vision
Togo = arrangement of words
Zo = image(s)
Zuno = brain

headers.Subject: Re: A Few Replies to a Few Comments...
